title: When the Archive Sings
premise: Wendell Montrose, last caretaker of the Meridian Seed Vault, records Earth's forgotten decline in audio logs no one answers. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, she decodes it as a plea from a colony ship the fleet declared lost — and discovers the fleet's fragile truce depends on that ship staying lost. Wendell must smuggle the message to both war fleets before the truce expires, exposing her own archive's role in the original betrayal. In the end she broadcasts the truth to everyone at once, ending the war by making denial impossible, and the vault becomes a listening post where the extinct language is spoken again.
about_author: Wren Voss is a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing dead broadcasts before turning to fiction. They write from a converted signal station on the coast, still convinced every silence contains a message.

chapters.title: The Quiet Inventory
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She catalogs the vault's dying systems and records her 4,000th unanswered log entry. The emotional beat is lonely devotion — she tends a monument to a world that stopped listening.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A burst transmission arrives in Old Meridian, a language extinct since the First Dispersal. She recognizes it from her grandmother's lullabies. Beat: wonder cracking through isolation.

chapters.title: What the Vault Remembers
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Digging through sealed archive strata, she finds the signal matches a colony ship, the Halcyon Reach, officially 'lost' two centuries ago. Beat: first unease — the loss was recorded too neatly.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Long Silence
chapters.summary: POV shift to Commander Ilsa Reyes aboard the fleet flagship Vigilant, holding a tenuous truce with the Breakaway flotilla. Beat: exhaustion and dread; the truce expires in nineteen days.

chapters.title: A Voice That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The signal repeats with new fragments: the Halcyon Reach is alive, decaying, and asking for help by name — hers. Beat: vertigo of being summoned by history.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Fleet intelligence intercepts the same signal and orders it buried; Reyes quietly keeps a copy. Beat: loyalty to the fleet begins to strain against something like conscience.

chapters.title: Decoding the Lullaby
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Using her grandmother's recordings as a cipher key, she translates the full plea — and a warning: the fleet knew the Reach survived. Beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Visitor
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A fleet retrieval team arrives at the vault, officially to 'audit' it. Wendell hides the decoded message inside seed-catalog audio files. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension in the stacks.

chapters.title: Auditor Kade
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. The auditor suspects Wendell but hesitates, haunted by a sister lost in the Breakaway war. Beat: the antagonist revealed as a person, not an instrument.

chapters.title: Seeds and Secrets
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She smuggles a copy of the message to a passing freighter pilot, Tam, an old friend of the vault. Beat: fragile trust; belonging tested by risk.

chapters.title: The Breakaway Listens
chapters.summary: POV shift to Sef Oyelaran, Breakaway flotilla leader, who receives Tam's transmission. Beat: hope and fury — the Reach carried Breakaway's founding families.

chapters.title: Thirteen Days
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Fleet command moves to silence the vault; Reyes must choose between her career and the truth she's been sitting on. Beat: the loyalty-vs-truth axis turns explicit.

chapters.title: Burn the Archive
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Kade returns with orders to purge the vault's signal records. Wendell triggers the vault's ancient failsafe: every seed vault on the network begins broadcasting her logs. Beat: defiant escalation.

chapters.title: The Network Wakes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided — Wendell, Reyes, Kade, Sef. The broadcast reaches both fleets simultaneously. Beat: chaos, denial, and the truce clock accelerating.

chapters.title: What We Buried
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. Confronted with the archive's proof, Kade defects, handing Wendell the fleet's internal orders. Beat: guilt transmuted into action; an unlikely alliance.

chapters.title: Run for the Reach
chapters.summary: Wendell and Kade flee the vault aboard Tam's freighter, pursued by both fleets, toward the Halcyon Reach's drifting coordinates. Beat: momentum and terror; the caretaker leaves her garden.

chapters.title: The Dying Ship
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They board the Reach: two hundred descendants of the 'lost,' alive but failing, speaking Old Meridian. Beat: awe and heartbreak — history has a face.

chapters.title: Four Days
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Both fleets converge on the Reach's position; the truce expires in four days. Reyes transmits Wendell's full logs to her own crew, breaking ranks. Beat: sacrifice of certainty.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She records the final message — the truth of the betrayal, the Reach's survival, the fleet's cover-up — and prepares to broadcast on all channels. Beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: Every Channel Open
chapters.summary: Climax, braided POVs. The broadcast hits both fleets mid-standoff; weapons arm, then waver as crews recognize their own dead in the archive's voice. Kade takes a hit shielding the transmitter. Beat: the war held at the edge of firing.

chapters.title: The Truce That Held
chapters.summary: Reyes's and Sef's POVs. Shamed and unmasked, both fleets stand down; the Reach's survivors are received as kin by both sides. Kade survives, wounded. Beat: release after unbearable tension.

chapters.title: When the Archive Sings
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, coda. The vault becomes a listening post and school where Old Meridian is taught again; Wendell records her 5,000th log — and this time, thousands answer. Beat: belonging earned, memory made living.
